items.title: Prism faces and a net
items.student: All dimensions in cm. A closed rectangular prism has length 8,width 5,height 3. List its six faces,draw a net and find total surface area. A right triangular prism has length 10 and a right-triangle cross-section with perpendicular legs 3 and 4,hypotenuse 5. List its two triangle and three rectangle faces;draw a net or a labelled face inventory and calculate total surface area. Nets need not be drawn to full scale;dimensions,not print measurements,govern. Explain why adding edge lengths is not surface area.
items.teacher: Rectangular faces:two 8×5,two 8×3,two 5×3;area 2(40+24+15)=158 cm². Triangular prism:two triangles area 6 each;rectangles 10×3,10×4,10×5;area 12+30+40+50=132 cm². A non-overlapping attached-face net or correctly labelled inventory is acceptable. Area counts square units,not total length. If making a paper model prepare ruler,paper and permitted supervised scissors or pre-cut pieces;this task does not promise a downloadable exact-scale template.

items.title: Right square pyramid: height or slant height?
items.student: A right square pyramid has base edge 6 cm,vertical height 4 cm and face slant height 5 cm measured from the apex to the midpoint of a base edge. Draw/label one triangular face and the central cross-section. Find total surface area of the closed pyramid. Explain why vertical height 4 cannot replace face slant height 5 in the four face triangles. Sketch a net with one 6×6 square and four triangles of base 6,perpendicular face altitude 5;label that altitude,not a sloping edge.
items.teacher: Each triangular face area(1/2)×6×5=15 cm²;four faces 60 plus base 36 gives 96 cm². Central right triangle has legs 4 and 3 and hypotenuse 5.5 is not the sloping apex-to-corner edge,which is√34 cm. The apex is directly above the square centre. Accurate labelling avoids confusing face altitude,solid vertical height and edge;physical construction is optional and does not substitute for individual area work.

items.title: Closed cylinder and cone surfaces
items.student: A right circular cone has radius 3 cm,vertical height 4 cm and slant height 5 cm. Find curved and total surface areas. Compare with a closed cylinder having the same radius and height. Identify which circular bases are included. Explain why cone slant height rather than vertical height appears in curved area. Optional net drawing:a radius 5 sector with central angle 216° and one radius 3 disk;verify that its curved edge fits the base circumference. Use dimensions as stated,not a guessed scale.
items.teacher: Cone curvedπrl=15π cm²;totalπrl+πr²=24π≈75.398 cm². Cylinder curved 2πrh=24π;two bases 18π;total 42π≈131.947 cm². The cone surface unrolls to a sector of radius l;216/360×2π5=6π,matching base circumference 2π3. Its sector area 216/360×π25=15π. A cylinder side unwraps to a rectangle height 4 and width 6π. These are ideal thin surfaces;open vessels omit the appropriate base.

items.title: Right circular frustum surface by subtraction
items.student: A cone is cut by a plane parallel to its base. The remaining right circular frustum has bottom radius 5 cm,top radius 2 cm,vertical height 4 cm and slant height 5 cm. Find the curved area and total area including both circular ends. Explain the small-cone subtraction that produces the curved-area formulaπ(R+r)s. Use similar triangles to find the original cone’s vertical/slant heights and the removed cone’s heights. Cross-section:two parallel diameter segments 10 and 4 cm,vertical separation 4 cm;each sloping side length 5 cm.
items.teacher: Original vertical height 20/3 cm,removed 8/3;original slant 25/3,removed 10/3 by similar cones. Curved areaπ[5(25/3)−2(10/3)]=35π cm²=π(5+2)5. End areas 25π+4π=29π;closed total 64π≈201.062 cm². Slant s²=h²+(R−r)²=16+9=25. Curved area is notπ(R−r)s or the area of a full cone of height 4. A frustum net’s curved part is an annular sector,not an ordinary trapezium.

items.title: Sphere surface and the limits of a flat net
items.student: For an ideal sphere radius 2 cm,use total surface area 4πr² to calculate its area. Compare a hemisphere’s curved area with its total area including the flat circular face. An illustration cuts a sphere into many narrow orange-peel-like strips. Is this an exact flat net like a prism net? Explain what such a model can illustrate and what it cannot prove. If radius doubles to 4 cm,predict and check the surface-area scale factor. Use a ball/paper sketch only;no cutting of a real ball is required.
items.teacher: Sphere area 16π≈50.265 cm². Hemisphere curved 8π;including flat disk adds 4π for total 12π cm². Radius 4 sphere 64π,area factor 4. A curved sphere has no exact distortion-free planar net made from ordinary flat faces;strips give an approximation or illustration,not an exact unfolding/proof. State 4πr² as the mathematical model here and use proportional/magnitude checks. Do not confuse the surface 4πr² with projected circleπr².

items.title: Composite surface: which faces become internal?
items.student: A rectangular box 8×6×4 cm is joined to a smaller box 2×2×3 cm along a complete 2×2 cm face with no volume overlap. Find exposed total surface area. Then consider a closed-bottom cylinder radius 3 cm,height 4 cm with a hemisphere of radius 3 cm attached at its top. The joining disks are internal. Find exposed total area,including the cylinder’s bottom but excluding both joined disks. Draw an inventory of exposed and hidden faces. Optional extension:a radius 1 cm cylindrical hole passes straight through opposite faces of a 6 cm cube. Which new curved surface is exposed?
items.teacher: Large box surface 208 cm²,small 32;subtract two contact faces 2×4=8,so 232 cm². Cylinder+hemisphere exposed 2πrh+2πr²+πr²=24π+18π+9π=51π≈160.221 cm². Adding standalone closed surfaces would wrongly count joined disks. For the through-hole cube,original 216 minus two circular openings 2π plus inner curved wall 2π×1×6=12π gives 216+10π cm². Extension is a paper geometry model only,no drilling. No trapped surface is counted as external.

items.title: Prism volume,capacity and internal dimensions
items.student: A right triangular prism has cross-section legs 3 and 4 cm and length 10 cm. Find its volume and distinguish it from the 132 cm² surface area in SV1. A closed storage box has internal dimensions 20×15×10 cm;find capacity in cm³ and litres using 1000 cm³=1 L. A label gives only external dimensions of a thick-walled container:can these alone determine usable capacity? Explain. For a cylinder radius 3 cm,height 4 cm,find volume as base area×perpendicular height.
items.teacher: Triangular base area 6 cm²×length 10 gives 60 cm³. Internal box 3000 cm³=3 L;usable capacity needs internal dimensions/shape and may differ from nominal fill space. External dimensions alone omit wall thickness/internal geometry. Cylinder 9π×4=36π≈113.097 cm³. A right-prism volume is cross-section area times perpendicular length;surface area and capacity use different quantities and units.1000 cm³=1 L and 1 cm³=1 mL;dimensions must share a unit before multiplying.

items.title: Cone,pyramid and a one-third volume model
items.student: For a right cone radius 3 cm,height 4 cm,calculate volume using(1/3)×base area×perpendicular height. For the square pyramid in SV2,calculate volume. Compare each with a cylinder/prism of the same base area and perpendicular height. Optional teacher-prepared demonstration:use a stable plastic cone and cylinder with the same measured internal radius and height,clean water and a spill tray;count approximately how many full cones fill the cylinder. Record what was actually done. Printed fallback,illustrative only:cone capacity 25.1 mL,cylinder 75.3 mL. Compute the ratio and discuss what one such comparison can/cannot establish. No unsealed paper model is used for pouring.
items.teacher: Cone(1/3)π9×4=12π≈37.699 cm³,one third of matching cylinder 36π. Square pyramid(1/3)36×4=48 cm³,one third of matching prism 144. Printed 75.3/25.1=3;this is consistent with the model,not a proof for every cone/pyramid. Use perpendicular height,not cone/pyramid slant height. Teacher prechecks equal internal bases/heights and water safety,uses nonbreakable vessels,keeps water away from electricity and cleans spills. Never cut household containers or use unknown substances. If models/access are unavailable use printed comparison and mark filling/measuring/model-making not observed;individual numerical explanation remains assessable. Record each actual participant’s action separately from group work.

items.title: Frustum volume by subtracting cones
items.student: Use the right circular frustum from SV4:R5 cm,r 2 cm,h 4 cm. From similar cones recover original/removed heights,then subtract their volumes. Compare withV=(πh/3)(R²+Rr+r²). Explain why simply subtracting two cylinders of height 4 gives the wrong solid. Check the frustum’s volume lies between cylinders of radius 2 and radius 5 with the same height 4.
items.teacher: Original H20/3,removed 8/3. Volume difference(π/3)[25(20/3)−4(8/3)]=52π≈163.363 cm³. Formula gives(4π/3)(25+10+4)=52π. Cylinder bound 16π<52π<100π. The changing cross-section radius is not represented by an annulus of constant thickness extruded through height 4;that mistaken expression would give 84π. Similar cone heights differ by 4.

items.title: Sphere and hemisphere volumes
items.student: UseV=(4/3)πr³ for a sphere radius 2 cm;find its volume exactly and approximately. Find the volume of a solid hemisphere of that radius. Compare with the volume of a sphere radius 4 cm and explain the radius scale factor. A claim says “a sphere’s 4πr² surface area is also its capacity”. Correct the units and reasoning. Distinguish a solid’s volume from a thick shell’s usable internal capacity.
items.teacher: Sphere 32π/3≈33.510 cm³;hemisphere 16π/3≈16.755 cm³. Radius 4 sphere 256π/3,volume factor 8;surface area scales by 4 instead. Surface units cm²,volume cm³. A hollow container’s capacity depends on internal radius,not merely an outer surface or outer radius. The formula is stated as the mathematical model here;an approximate physical comparison illustrates rather than proves it. No unsafe sphere cutting is required.

items.title: Composite volume: add joined parts,subtract a cavity
items.student: First find volume of the joined 8×6×4 and 2×2×3 cm boxes in SV6;they touch but do not overlap in volume. Then find volume of a cylinder radius 3 cm,height 4 cm topped by a solid hemisphere radius 3 cm. Finally,a 6 cm cube has a radius 1 cm straight cylindrical hole through its full 6 cm length:find remaining solid volume. State what is added/removed and why touching face area is not a volume correction. These are paper models;no drilling or cutting real objects.
items.teacher: Joined boxes 192+12=204 cm³;there is no overlapping 3 D region to subtract. Cylinder 36π plus hemisphere(2/3)π27=18π gives 54π≈169.646 cm³. Holed cube 216−π1²6=216−6π≈197.150 cm³. Surface contact requires area subtraction in SV6;zero-thickness contact planes have zero 3 D volume. If solids actually overlapped in a volume,this would need separate removal. Treat dimensions and cavity direction as given.

items.title: Choose area or volume for the decision
items.student: Fictional ideal container:an open-top cylinder has internal radius 4 cm,height 10 cm;ignore wall thickness solely for this model. Find material area for side+bottom and capacity in litres. Material costs a stated 0.5 KES per cm²;find the model cost before any waste/joining allowance. Explain why that price estimate is not a complete real purchasing quotation. Compare with incorrectly including a lid. State one local application of surface area and one of volume/capacity.
items.teacher: Side 80π plus base 16π=96π≈301.593 cm². Capacity 160π cm³≈502.655 mL≈0.503 L. Model material cost 48π≈150.796 KES,or 150.80 to 2 decimal places. A lid would add 16π cm² and 8π KES;it is omitted because the design is open. Real estimates need external dimensions/thickness,joining/cutting/waste,price validity and relevant additional costs;do not invent a percentage allowance or market price. Surface quantity models covering material;volume models internal space.

items.title: A usable solid model with an honest evidence record
items.student: Choose a safe paper model/net of a prism or pyramid from SV1/SV2,or a clean teacher-provided container. Label dimensions,identify which surfaces are exposed and calculate area/volume under stated assumptions. If measuring a real container,state whether dimensions are internal/external and record the instrument/precision;if using a drawing,label it a diagram calculation. Compare with a peer’s model and correct one claim. Audit:A a cone radius 3,height 4 has curved area 12π;B a pyramid’s volume uses face slant height;C joining two solid boxes requires subtracting their contact area from their total volume. Give a reasoned practical benefit and a safe next investigation. Construction uses school-provided paper/tools;home materials are not required.
items.teacher: A false:curved area 15π uses slant 5;12π is the cone volume coefficient with cm³,not curved cm². B false:perpendicular height is required. C false:contact area is not a 3 D overlap;volume adds if they only touch. Each chosen model must supply enough data;accept a drawn route but record physical measuring/making not observed there. Prepare ruler,compass/protractor if relevant,paper and permitted supervised scissors/pre-cut alternative. No blades,throwing,unknown containers,heating or risky outdoor measurement. Record individual reasoning,actual actions and peer collaboration separately;neat decoration is not mathematical evidence.

items.title: Independent solids data and formula support
items.student: All lengths in cm;dimensions exact;schematic drawings are not to scale. F a closed right circular frustum:R6,r 3,vertical h 4,slant s 5. G a right cylinder radius 2,height 6,closed at bottom,with a solid hemisphere radius 2 attached at the top;the two joined disks are internal. H a rectangular container has internal dimensions 25×12×8 cm. Useπ calculator value;give exact forms where appropriate and approximate final values to 3 decimal places. Support:circleπr²;trianglebh/2;cone curvedπrl;frustum curvedπ(R+r)s;hemisphere curved 2πr²;prism/cylinder volumeAh;cone/pyramidAh/3;frustum volume(πh/3)(R²+Rr+r²);sphere volume 4πr³/3;1 L=1000 cm³. Add only exposed faces;show your decomposition.
items.teacher: Release only in Lesson 14 with separate task prompts. F total surfaceπ(6+3)5+π36+π9=90π≈282.743 cm²;volume(4π/3)(36+18+9)=84π≈263.894 cm³. G exposed area 2π2×6+2π2²+π2²=36π≈113.097 cm²;volumeπ4×6+(2/3)π8=88π/3≈92.153 cm³. H2400 cm³=2.4 L;externaldimensions alone would not establish this capacity. Formula support does not include solved answers or substitute for explanation. Practical final response has no unique price/waste value;judge a supported use,missingdatum,unit and safe next step.
